_comment_h6: Bug-1 canonical reproducer (David Dai R1 distilled). cpu.max=10000 100000 (10% of one CPU), 16 oversubscribed yes-loop workers (4x nproc with nr_cpus=4). The simulator-only knobs (LAVD enable_cpu_bw, watchdog timeout, scheduler selection) come from the scxsim CLI / config sidecar (bug1_canonical.toml + --watchdog 80ms -s lavd --cpus 4 --duration 500ms). See experiments/lavd_cpubw_stalls_202604/davids-artifacts/lavd_bw_repro_r1_tight.sh and SCXSIM_CGROUP_BW_DESIGN.md.
_comment_caveat: SHAPE-of-stall reproducer, NOT a faithful production-mechanism reproducer. The intended invocation uses --watchdog 80ms (< period 100ms), so the watchdog provably fires before the first refill at t=100ms can be reached by the engine event loop. With realistic settings (--watchdog 5s --duration 10s), the same workload's max stall is ~200ms (2 periods) — refill works, no multi-second stall. So this fixture demonstrates the SHAPE of Bug-1 (oversubscribed cgroup → throttle → tasks pile up → watchdog fires) but does NOT model the production mechanism (≥30s stalls under the kernel's 30s watchdog default with refill firing every 100ms). See experiments/lavd_cpubw_stalls_202604/overnight_2026-05-08/STREAM_C_FOLLOWUP_REFILL_INVESTIGATION.md §5-6 for the full evidence.
_comment_run_units: rt-app 'run' is microseconds. 200000us = 200ms per task per loop iteration, matching the prior library-form scenario builder's REPRO_TASK_RUN_NS = 200_000_000ns.
